# Ty Masterson Watchdog File

**Subject:** Ty Masterson, Republican nominee for governor of Kansas, 2026, president of the Kansas Senate from Andover
**Compiled:** October 27, 2026 for the On Point Politics watchdog database, onpointpolitics.us
**Data cutoff:** July 23, 2026 for state ethics commission filings. Outside spending through October 26, 2026.
**Next scheduled data drop:** The Kansas pre-general candidate report due October 26, 2026, which was not yet retrieved for this file.

## Bottom line up front

Masterson won a seven candidate Republican primary on August 4, 2026 with 43 percent, carried by President Trump's endorsement, per the Kansas Reflector on October 20, 2026, https://www.newsfromthestates.com/article/trump-affirms-endorsement-ty-masterson-kansas-governors-race-belittles-cindy-holscher. Trump reaffirmed it at a Park City rally on October 19.

His July report shows $766,535.24 raised from January 1 to July 23, 2026, $1,023,845.63 spent, and $430,211.71 left, per his filing, https://www.kansas.gov/ethics/CFAScanned/StWide/2026ElecCycle/202607/SW01TM_202607.pdf. That is about $365,000 more cash than Holscher held on the same date.

Three interests combine money and a decision:

1. **The RGA.** Right Direction PAC reserved about $6.9 million against Holscher.
2. **The data center and AI industry.** Building the Future, an offshoot of Leading the Future, is spending more than $1.5 million for him. He voted for SB 98, the 20 year data center sales tax exemption, and defends it.
3. **Agriculture.** The Kansas Farm Bureau PAC, the Kansas Grain and Feed Association and the Kansas Agribusiness Retailers Association endorsed him. The lever is the property tax cap.

## Committee structure and treasurer

The candidate committee files as Ty Masterson for Governor, filer code SW01TM, with Tom Devlin as treasurer. His nonprofit, Take Back Kansas, entered 2026 with $700,000, per the Kansas Reflector on January 19, 2026, https://www.newsfromthestates.com/article/millionaire-candidates-kansas-governor-burnish-fundraising-personal-loans. That article does not say whether the nonprofit is tied to the campaign. His running mate is Sen. Jeff Klemp of Leavenworth.

Vendors on the July report: Brabender Cox for radio and TV placement, $200,000 on June 4 and further payments the scan shows as about $383,787 and a $208,802 commission, and LW Gillis & Co for fundraising, about $32,601. Only the $200,000 line parsed cleanly.

## Bloc: Party and leadership

Documented. Right Direction PAC reserved about $6.9 million from the end of the primary through the general, per the Sunflower State Journal on August 5, 2026, https://sunflowerstatejournal.com/national-republican-take-offensive-in-kansas-governors-race/. Its ads hit Holscher on property taxes, California and trans care. In the primary, three groups booked a little over $1 million in one day on June 23, 2026, including Farmers First Fund, a Virginia entity with no listed officers that was expected to back him, and a PAC linked to Masterson.

Inference: The RGA reservation is about two and a half times the DGA's KVI reservation, so the outside money gap favors him more than the candidate cash gap does.

## Bloc: AI industry and data centers

Documented. Building the Future is spending more than $1.5 million for him, per a person familiar who spoke to NBC News on October 26, 2026, https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/data-center-group-jumps-kansas-205208816.html. Leading the Future is funded heavily by Marc Andreessen, Ben Horowitz and OpenAI's Greg Brockman, per TechCrunch on August 31, 2026. NetChoice requested the bill that became SB 98, and NetChoice president Steve DelBianco gave Masterson $8,000, per the Kansas Reflector on October 9, 2026, https://www.hppr.org/hppr-news/2026-10-12/debate-about-kansas-law-incentivizing-data-center-construction-charges-up-governors-race. Holscher claims IT and AI interests have put nearly $1 million into his campaign. That claim was not checked against filings. Evergy Metro gave $4,000 on July 23, 2026.

What they want. Keep the SB 98 exemption and local siting control. He says data centers should pay full electricity costs in every KCC rate case, opposes eminent domain for them, and wants a security review to block Chinese technology.

Inference: His ratepayer pledge answers the attack without touching the tax break the industry values most.

## Bloc: Agriculture and allied labor

Documented. Kansas Farm Bureau PAC, the Kansas Grain and Feed Association and the Kansas Agribusiness Retailers Association endorsed him, along with SMART Transportation Division, IBEW Local 124 and the Kansas State Council of Fire Fighters, per the Kansas Reflector on October 12, 2026, https://kansasreflector.com/2026/10/12/cindy-holscher-ty-masterson-gain-gubernatorial-endorsements-from-labor-ag-interests/. His property tax plan caps growth in taxable assessed value at 3 percent or less a year by constitutional amendment.

Inference: A valuation cap protects existing farm and home owners most, and critics say it shifts the burden to new buyers and commercial property.

## Positions and record

He served in the House from 2005 to 2009, in the Senate since, and as Senate president since 2021. He negotiated the 2024 tax plan with Speaker Dan Hawkins and Gov. Laura Kelly, voted to bar transgender girls from girls' sports, and blocked university diversity programs, per KCUR on October 14, 2026. He backs tax credit scholarships and a Mississippi style literacy push. He declined further televised debates.

## Own finances and disclosure history

He is director of GoCreate, a Wichita State University makerspace KWCH describes as Koch Foundation funded. His salary was $163,000 in 2025 and $217,350 in 2026 per the WSU budget, per KWCH on July 13, 2026, https://www.kwch.com/2026/07/14/not-once-have-i-ever-seen-him-questions-mount-over-ty-mastersons-217k-job-wsu-makerspace/. Reports put his GoCreate pay at more than $1 million since 2017. He took unpaid leave from August 17, 2026, and his spokesman says he will leave the post on taking office. His legislative salary is about $85,000, per Holscher and the DGA. He was a contractor and owner of Masterbuilt homes and filed personal bankruptcy in 2010 after it failed. No statement of substantial interests was retrieved.

## Enforcement and controversies

- **GoCreate no-show charge. Contested.** Rivals and the DGA call it a no-show job. WSU says his duties go beyond office presence. Masterson says the work is administrative and he is on site two or three days a week at times.
- **State ethics complaint. Dismissed.** Former Sen. Mark Steffan, a Sarnecki backer, alleged campaigning on public time. The state commission dismissed it before the primary. The campaign called it bunk, per KWCH on August 11, 2026.
- **Brownback quote. Contested.** A DGA ad quotes him saying he wrote the Brownback plan. He says the clip was chopped and referred to a 2007 or 2008 ratchet idea. An Emporia State expert says he shepherded the plan but did not write it.

## Deal table

| Interest | Money in | Ask | Lever | Stake | Decision date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RGA | About $6.9M reserved | Flip the seat | Governor plus GOP supermajority | Not quantified | November 3, 2026 |
| AI and data centers | Building the Future $1.5M plus; DelBianco $8,000 | Keep SB 98; local control | Veto over any pause | At least a dozen proposals | 2027 session |
| Agriculture | Endorsements; dollar gifts not verified | Property tax cap | Constitutional amendment | Not quantified | 2027 session |
| Koch funded GoCreate | $217,350 salary in 2026 | Not stated | WSU budget | Not quantified | January 2027 |

## Levers and calendar

| Decision | Who holds it now | When | Which donors care |
|---|---|---|---|
| Data center incentives and rate rules | Legislature; KCC | 2027 session | Building the Future; NetChoice; Evergy |
| Property tax cap amendment | Legislature, then voters | 2027 at the earliest | Farm Bureau; homeowners |
| Tax credit scholarships | Legislature | 2027 session | School choice and family |
| Abortion amendment | Legislature | Not scheduled | Kansans for Life PAC |
| Exit from GoCreate | WSU | January 2027 | Koch Foundation |

Calendar. The election is November 3, 2026. The new governor takes office in January 2027 with the 2027 session.

## What we could not verify

- Itemized donors above $4,000; Crossland related gifts on June 16 could not be matched to amounts. Most Brabender Cox amounts parsed from scanned text.
- The October 26 pre-general report.
- Take Back Kansas filings and donors; Farmers First Fund funders; Kansas Comeback PAC funders.
- The Koch Foundation's dollar support for GoCreate.
- His response to the bankruptcy attack. His statement of substantial interests.
- Bodies not read or only partly read: paywalled Sunflower State Journal stories of June 23, June 30, August 5, August 13 and September 29, 2026; the Kansas City Star GoCreate story, seen only as quoted by the DGA at https://democraticgovernors.org/updates/new-kansas-gop-candidate-ty-masterson-made-over-dollar1-million-from-megadonor-backed-organization-and-doesnt-even-show-up-to-work/; https://www.kctv5.com/video/2026/10/25/ty-masterson-discusses-his-campaign-governor-with-kctv5/ not viewed; the Washington Examiner report of his seven figure ad buy, seen only via https://www.multistate.us/elections/governor-race/kansas-2026.

# Ty Masterson research notes

Audit trail for KS-ty-masterson, compiled October 27, 2026. Searches shared with the Cindy Holscher file.

## Thread 1: Committees and totals

### Takeaway
$766,535.24 raised January 1 to July 23, 2026, $430,211.71 cash at the end, roughly $365,000 ahead of Holscher.

### Cited findings
- July 2026 report: treasurer Tom Devlin; beginning cash $687,522.10, receipts $766,535.24, expenditures $1,023,845.63, no loans, ending cash $430,211.71; Brabender Cox $200,000 on June 4; other Brabender Cox and LW Gillis lines parsed from jumbled scan text; $4,000 gifts from Evergy Metro, Cedars Inc., Patrick and Robyn Johnson, Stephen Clark. https://www.kansas.gov/ethics/CFAScanned/StWide/2026ElecCycle/202607/SW01TM_202607.pdf
- 2025: raised nearly $700,000, $687,000 cash, no loans; consultants replaced in late 2025; Take Back Kansas nonprofit entered 2026 with $700,000. https://www.newsfromthestates.com/article/millionaire-candidates-kansas-governor-burnish-fundraising-personal-loans

### Gaps
- Crossland related $4,000 entries on June 16 could not be matched; October 26 report; Take Back Kansas filings.

## Thread 2: Outside allies and opposition

### Cited findings
- RGA Right Direction PAC, about $6.9 million reserved against Holscher. https://sunflowerstatejournal.com/national-republican-take-offensive-in-kansas-governors-race/
- Building the Future, more than $1.5 million for him; Masterson did not immediately comment. https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/data-center-group-jumps-kansas-205208816.html
- Leading the Future funded by Andreessen, Horowitz and Brockman; Build American AI ads in Kansas. https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/31/a-group-funded-by-andreessen-horowitz-and-brockman-plan-data-center-ads-to-sway-midterms/
- Primary: three groups booked a little over $1 million on June 23, including Farmers First Fund. https://sunflowerstatejournal.com/republican-primary-heats-up-1-million-in-new-broadcast-spending-booked-in-a-day/
- Kansas Comeback PAC, Sarnecki affiliated, about $360,000 against him on June 30. https://sunflowerstatejournal.com/sarnecki-affiliated-pac-launches-assault-against-masterson/
- KVI for the DGA, $2.755 million reserved against him. https://sunflowerstatejournal.com/national-democrats-launch-first-ad-against-masterson-republicans-counter/
- DGA Brownback ad and his denial. https://www.hppr.org/hppr-news/2026-10-02/democrats-ad-links-ty-masterson-to-sam-brownback-kansas-gop-nominee-claims-its-a-lie

### Inferences
- Outside money favors him by roughly $4 million in reservations before counting Building the Future.

### Gaps
- Aired totals versus reservations; Farmers First Fund and Masterson linked PAC funders.

## Thread 3: GoCreate, ethics and finances

### Cited findings
- GoCreate salary $163,000 in 2025 and $217,350 in 2026; Koch Foundation funded per KWCH; WSU and campaign responses. https://www.kwch.com/2026/07/14/not-once-have-i-ever-seen-him-questions-mount-over-ty-mastersons-217k-job-wsu-makerspace/
- Steffan ethics complaint dismissed before the primary; campaign called it bunk. https://www.kwch.com/2026/08/11/update-ethics-complaint-against-ty-masterson-dismissed-order-confirms/
- Unpaid leave from August 17, 2026; more than $1 million from GoCreate since 2017; he will leave on taking office. https://sunflowerstatejournal.com/masterson-taking-leave-from-gocreate/
- DGA release quoting the Kansas City Star: $1.1 million from the WSU Foundation over ten years. https://democraticgovernors.org/updates/new-kansas-gop-candidate-ty-masterson-made-over-dollar1-million-from-megadonor-backed-organization-and-doesnt-even-show-up-to-work/
- Masterbuilt homes and 2010 bankruptcy; legislative history. https://www.kcur.org/politics-elections-and-government/2026-10-14/kansas-governor-race-2026-election-candidates-masterson-holscher

### Gaps
- Statement of substantial interests; his response to the bankruptcy attack.

## Thread 4: Positions and record

### Cited findings
- SB 98 vote April 11, 2025; ratepayer pledge; DelBianco $8,000; Holscher's nearly $1 million claim. https://www.hppr.org/hppr-news/2026-10-12/debate-about-kansas-law-incentivizing-data-center-construction-charges-up-governors-race
- 3 percent valuation cap, literacy, tax credit scholarships, no more debates. https://www.hppr.org/2026-10-13/in-race-for-kansas-governor-masterson-and-holscher-focus-on-taxes-and-education-funding
- Kansans for Life PAC endorsement; running mate Klemp. https://kansasreflector.com/?p=60370

## Campaign intel

- **Main message.** Property tax relief and affordability: no Kansan taxed out of a home, farm or business, a 3 percent cap on assessed value growth, and Holscher as too radical for Kansas. https://www.hppr.org/2026-10-13/in-race-for-kansas-governor-masterson-and-holscher-focus-on-taxes-and-education-funding and https://www.multistate.us/elections/governor-race/kansas-2026
- **Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it.** Brownback 2.0 plus a Koch funded GoCreate post paying $217,350 that rivals call a no-show job, along with big tech tax breaks and his 2010 bankruptcy; he denies writing the Brownback plan and WSU defends his role. https://www.hppr.org/hppr-news/2026-10-02/democrats-ad-links-ty-masterson-to-sam-brownback-kansas-gop-nominee-claims-its-a-lie and https://www.kwch.com/2026/07/14/not-once-have-i-ever-seen-him-questions-mount-over-ty-mastersons-217k-job-wsu-makerspace/
- **Strongest coalition.** Trump's base plus farm groups, with the Farm Bureau PAC, Kansas Grain and Feed and Agribusiness Retailers, and some building trades and transport unions. https://kansasreflector.com/2026/10/12/cindy-holscher-ty-masterson-gain-gubernatorial-endorsements-from-labor-ag-interests/
- **Weak spot in polling.** He is underwater at 40 favorable and 44 unfavorable while Holscher is net positive, and he led independents only 47 to 45 in Emerson's September 15 to 16 poll. https://emersoncollegepolling.com/kansas-2026/
- **Recent event.** Building the Future, a pro data center super PAC, put more than $1.5 million behind him on October 26, a week after Trump reaffirmed his endorsement at a Park City rally. https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/data-center-group-jumps-kansas-205208816.html and https://www.newsfromthestates.com/article/trump-affirms-endorsement-ty-masterson-kansas-governors-race-belittles-cindy-holscher
- **Money gap.** He held $430,211.71 on July 23 to Holscher's $64,933.65, and the RGA reserved about $6.9 million to the DGA's $2.755 million through KVI. https://www.kansas.gov/ethics/CFAScanned/StWide/2026ElecCycle/202607/SW01TM_202607.pdf and https://sunflowerstatejournal.com/national-republican-take-offensive-in-kansas-governors-race/
